title: A status change records who made it and when
custom_preconds:
Setup (manual QA tester and Claude session)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in as an Admin at {Location-A} (for example Staging Heavy Duty - 9919), a role that has 'Part Library & Inventory → View', 'Create & Edit' and 'Delete'.
  • Inventory part {Part-A} (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PL-WHOWHEN-01) is tracked at {Location-A} and is active.
  • Your name as Part History shows it is {Staff-A} (for example Admin ShopView).
  • Just before the change you note the computer clock's date and time as {Time-A} (for example 13 Oct 2026, 10:42 AM).
custom_steps:
1. Write down the date and time on your computer clock; this time is {Time-A}.
  2. On the Active tab search {Part-A}, click its row, pick Part Status "Inactive", click Save, leave the note empty and click "Deactivate" in the "Deactivate part?" confirmation.
  3. On the Inactive tab click the clock icon ("Part History") on {Part-A}'s row.
  4. Read the newest entry.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 4: The newest entry reads "Deactivated", with Staff {Staff-A}, today's Date, and a Time equal to {Time-A} or a minute or two later.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-10647; story SV-10823 (Story 10, Confirming and Recording a Status Change); PRD "Parts Lifecycle Update", Confluence 829227015, v29 (14 Oct 2026 copy), S10-R14, read 14 Oct 2026; design canvas board 3.8 (Finding it in Part History), 13 Oct copy. Source-verified 14 October 2026; not yet build-verified (no Part Lifecycle QA build exists).

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S10-R14: “Every status change records the user who made it, and the date and time.”
